canonical_name: Weak maximum principle for the heat equation
canonical_statement: Let U be a bounded open subset of Euclidean space, let T > 0, and let u be continuous on the closed space-time cylinder and twice continuously differentiable in space and once in time in its interior. If u_t - Laplacian u <= 0 in the cylinder, then the maximum of u on the closed cylinder equals its maximum on the parabolic boundary (initial time together with the lateral boundary).
domain_and_universes: Planned: finite-dimensional real Euclidean space; bounded open U; positive real T; scalar u on the closure of U x (0,T]
quantifiers: bounded open U subset of Real^n
u : closure(U x (0,T]) -> Real with the stated regularity
hypotheses: u is continuous on the closed cylinder
u has two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative in the interior
u_t - Laplacian u <= 0 in the interior
conclusion: max over the closed cylinder u = max over the parabolic boundary u

alternate_encodings.target: For every interior point (x,t), u(x,t) <= sup on the parabolic boundary u
alternate_encodings.relationship: iff subject to compactness and attainment
